events.title: Land is Power: Indigenous Sovereignty and Black Liberation
events.short_description: Wednesday, November 11th is Pan-African Community Action’s next Assata Shakur Popular Education session, " Land is Power: Indigenous Sovereignty and Black Liberation" an interactive discussion with multimedia presentation from 7 to 9 PM at the Black Workers & Wellness Center on 2500 Martin Luther King Jr Avenue, Southeast, DC. More information and registration is on "Popular Education [dot] Eventb
events.full_description: This session of Assata Shakur Popular Education (ASPE) will examine the history of Indigenous resistance to settler colonialism, the origins of private property, and the connections between Indigenous land struggles and broader African liberation movements. We will explore the contradictions between liberal reforms, land acknowledgments, and genuine land sovereignty, including the struggle for nationhood, self-determination, and community control. Through historical and contemporary examples, we will examine how displacement, environmental destruction, and the continued occupation of Indigenous lands sustain colonial relationships of power. Finally, we will connect these struggles to the conditions facing working- class Black communities in Southeast DC, exploring how the lack of community control over land shapes development, environmental conditions, public resources, and everyday life.  ASPEs are hybrid sessions and can be attended via Zoom. To receive the Zoom link register here https://Populareducation.eventbrite.com  Food and refreshments will be provided. All are welcome.
events.street_address: 2500 Martin Luther King Junior Avenue SE

events.title: Protect East Potomac Park Lobby Day
events.organization: U.S. Senator Ankit Jain, Washington Area Bicyclist Association, and Save East Po
events.short_description: Join us at Protect East Potomac Park Lobby Day! Community members and advocates will meet with congressional offices to urge lawmakers to disapprove a proposed $450 million in federal funding without clear and explicit prohibitions on any further redevelopment of East Potomac Park until the seawall construction is complete.
events.full_description: The Office of United States Senator Ankit Jain, the Washington Area Bicyclist Association (WABA), Save East Po, and other partner organizations will bring community members and advocates to Capitol Hill for a Lobby Day to protect East Potomac Park and Hains Point from the Trump administration’s proposed redevelopment.  In a June 24, 2026, funding request to Congress, the Trump administration requested $450 million for the National Park Service's construction account to rebuild the aging seawall surrounding East Potomac Park.  As Congress considers whether to include this request in an upcoming continuing resolution, advocates are urging lawmakers not to approve the funding without clear and explicit prohibitions on any further redevelopment of East Potomac Park until the seawall construction is complete.  Participants will meet with congressional offices throughout the day to urge lawmakers to protect East Potomac Park as an accessible, affordable, multi-use public space for everyone and ensure that federal funding cannot be diverted to support the President's proposed redevelopment.
events.funders: Office of U.S. Senator Ankit Jain (https://www.senatorjaindc.com/) Washington Area Bicyclist Association (WABA) (https://waba.org/) Save East Po (https://saveeastpo.com/)

events.title: LoveSound: An Evening of Soul Sisters in Performance
events.organization: Friends of the Congo, Africa World Now Project and WPFW
events.short_description: Friends of the Congo, Africa World Now Project and WPFW invite you to LoveSound: An Evening of Soul Sisters in Performance to benefit the women of the Congo and WPFW on Sunday, November 22, 5-8pm at Westminster Presbyterian Church - 400 I Street, SW, Washington.
events.full_description:
Friends of the Congo, Africa World Now Project and WPFW invite you to LoveSound: An Evening of Soul Sisters in Performance to benefit the women of the Congo and WPFW on Sunday, November 22, 5-8pm at Westminster Presbyterian Church - 400 I Street, SW, Washington. 

The evening features performances by musicians and poets including Free BenJamin, Wayna, Anna Mwalagho, Ayanna Gregory, Navasha Daya, Laini Mataka, Janelle Gill, CeLilliane Green and Sweet Honey In the Rock.

This will be an evening of upliftment of the displaced women and children in the Basandja Coalition, which constitutes local and Indigenous communities on the frontlines in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

events.title: WPFW 50th Anniversary Gala
events.short_description: An evening honoring five decades of community-powered radio: music, guest speakers, special tributes, and the people who have kept 89.3 on the air since 1977. Tickets on sale in November.
events.full_description:
WPFW turns fifty on February 28, 2027, and this is the night the station marks it. An evening of music, guest speakers and special tributes at Martin's Crosswinds in Greenbelt, Maryland.

Some of the people in that room signed the station on in 1977. Some found 89.3 last week on a car radio. It is the first real chance in a long time to get listeners, volunteers, programmers and staff under one roof.

Tickets go on sale in November. The start time will be announced here and on the air.
